chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu al-Maghra, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made the rich and the poor partners in the wealth; therefore, it is not for them to direct it to other than their partners.
ai.seo_question: Why can't Zakat be given to the rich according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the concept of 'shirk' (partnership) in wealth, establishing that the poor have a divinely ordained right in the assets of the wealthy, thereby transforming Zakat from mere charity into a fulfillment of rights. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on verifying the recipient's actual financial status to prevent the misappropriation of communal funds, ensuring the distribution aligns with the Quranic mandate of purifying wealth through rightful allocation.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abu Al Magra, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and high Associated between the rich and the poor in the wealth. Thus, it is not for them that they should be disbursing it upon other than their associates’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from abu al-Maghra’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Allah, most Blessed, most High, has made the affluent to share their wealth with the needy people; thus, they must not share it with others (affluent ones).”’
